verdict.rationale: Obsidian stores the whole vault as non-proprietary plain-text Markdown files on the user's device, so the knowledge base is always available in an open format. The docs say this lets you switch to another app easily, and community switchers corroborate owning their files and expecting them to outlive Obsidian. Missing for 10: a documented bulk-export workflow (exit relies on the files already being on disk), Wikilinks being non-standard by default (Markdown links require an opt-in setting), and no evidence on how app-specific files such as JSON .canvas files carry over to other tools.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can export my entire knowledge base at any time in open formats, so leaving is as easy as arriving

citations.quote: Obsidian uses non-proprietary plain text Markdown files stored locally on your device. You have total control over your data, which means you can use Obsidian offline and switch to another app easily
Obsidian stores your notes as Markdown-formatted plain text files in a vault.
Because notes are plain text files, you can use other text editors and file managers to edit and manage notes.
If interoperability is important to you, you can disable Wikilinks and use Markdown links instead.
as plain text they can outlive Obsidian itself
